A Coffee Purist’s Haven in a Serene Locale.

Blue Tokai in Breach Candy is less of a typical café and more of a sanctuary for serious coffee lovers. Located on a quiet, leafy lane, it provides an escape from the city’s hustle without compromising on a world-class caffeine fix.

The Coffee & Food (4.5/5):
The coffee is, of course, the hero. I ordered a pour-over of their seasonal roast (a Kenyan) and a flat white. Both were brewed to perfection – balanced, aromatic, and showcasing the beans’ distinct notes. The baristas are knowledgeable and happy to explain the profiles. The food menu is thoughtfully curated to complement the coffee. The Avocado & Feta Toast on sourdough was fresh and satisfying, and the Almond Croissant was flaky and buttery. featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Excelsior is one of those heritage Irani cafés that carries decades of nostalgia with it. In its prime, it was a landmark dining spot in Fort — a place where classic Parsi and Irani flavours defined comfort food for generations. On our recent visit, however, the experience felt more like a reminder of its glorious past rather than its present strength.

We ordered the Bun Maska with Chai, which remains a simple, comforting classic. The chai had that familiar strong brew, and the bun maska did evoke a bit of old-school charm. The Mutton Cutlet one of their most talked-about dishes — was decent, with the cutlet nicely fried, though the gravy lacked the richness we had expected from all the praise it receives. The Kheema pav and kheema Ghotala was flavourful and satisfying, pairing well with pav, and probably one of the better dishes of our meal.

The menu itself is extensive and filled with iconic dishes like Mutton Pattice, Sali Boti, Chicken and Mutton Dhansak, Kheema Pav, Chicken Roll, Mutton Burger, and even hearty plates like Triple Fried Rice. Their dessert section still showcases classics such as Caramel Custard and Bread Pudding, along with nostalgic beverages like Raspberry Soda and Ice-Cream Soda — all of which reflect the café’s rich culinary history.

However, beyond the food, there were noticeable gaps in the overall experience. The service was considerably slow despite the place not being overly crowded. Hygiene and upkeep could definitely use more attention — from table cleanliness to the general maintenance of the space. For a café with such a legacy, these details matter.

Cafe Excelsior undoubtedly holds historical value and sentimental charm, and it’s easy to imagine how special it must have felt in its prime years. Today, while the food is still reasonably good and certain dishes retain their nostalgic appeal, the overall experience feels like it needs revival and renewed care.

With some focused improvements in service speed, consistency, and hygiene, this iconic café could very well reclaim a bit of its old magic. For now, it remains a place worth visiting once for the heritage factor — but perhaps not quite the culinary standout it used to be.

The gravy, despite being a Parsi one, weirdly felt so close to home. I had it sparingly so that I could enjoy it the day after, too. Highly recommend their cutlets. featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
An unforgettable Thai brunch experience that truly transported us straight to the bustling streets of Bangkok 🇹🇭✨
We recently attended the Tuk Tuk Tales pop-up at Plate & Pint curated by the incredibly talented Chef Akanksha Saigal, and every single dish on the menu reflected her passion, creativity, and deep understanding of authentic Thai flavours.
We went as a group of friends for brunch, and honestly, it turned into one of those meals where every plate sparks conversation, every bite feels memorable, and time just flies by over great food and even better company. The vibe at Plate & Pint added so much warmth to the experience — lively, cozy, vibrant, and perfect for a long indulgent afternoon.
The meal began with the Mango & Avocado Ceviche — incredibly fresh, bright, and beautifully balanced with chilli, lime, cilantro, green apple, and crispy shallots adding layers of texture and zing. A refreshing start that instantly awakened the palate.
The Crispy Potato Stacks were an absolute standout. Perfectly crisp with rich green curry notes, aromatic fried basil, chilli crackling, and toasted herb rice bringing together comfort and complexity in every bite.
The Gai Yang Thai BBQ Chicken was beautifully charred and deeply flavourful, paired wonderfully with pickled cucumber, pickled chilli, and a delicious dipping sauce that elevated the smokiness of the chicken.
The Spicy Tamarind Glaze dishes were another highlight. Both the cottage cheese and pork belly versions were packed with bold sweet spicy flavours and had that addictive Thai style balance that keeps you reaching for another bite.
For mains, the Holy Basil Stir Fry was pure comfort food done right. Fragrant basil, juicy chicken, cucumber, fluffy rice, and a fried egg made this dish hearty, satisfying, and incredibly soulful.
The Tom Yum Hot Pot was bursting with authentic Thai aromatics — lemongrass, galangal, lime leaf — with the prawns soaking beautifully in the deeply comforting broth. Warm, sharp, spicy, and layered with flavour.
And of course, no Thai meal feels complete without a great Pad Thai, and this one absolutely delivered. Perfectly cooked rice noodles coated in tamarind sauce with chicken, bean sprouts, and peanuts creating the ideal balance of sweet, savoury, nutty, and tangy flavours.
Dessert was the perfect finale — Mango Sticky Rice with tender coconut ice cream. Rich, fragrant, comforting, and tropical all at once. Easily one of the best versions we’ve had in Mumbai.
The cocktails were equally thoughtful and fun, especially the Thai Chilli Guava Michelada and Mango Chilli White Wine Spritz, which paired beautifully with the food and added another vibrant layer to the entire experience.
Huge compliments to Chef Akanksha for creating such a well executed pop-up that didn’t just serve food, but genuinely told a story through flavours. Every dish felt curated with heart and authenticity.
Thank you for inviting us and giving us such a memorable afternoon filled with laughter, amazing conversations, delicious food, and beautiful hospitality. Experiences like these are exactly why food brings people together so effortlessly.

Already looking forward to the next one ❤️
